Hi Sara —

Great to speak earlier. Quick recap from our discovery on SLOs and the dedicated capacity validation we discussed, plus proposed next steps so we can align scope before engineering validation: 

High-level SLOs you called out:
- P95 token-latency target for generation (streaming) = 150ms or better for 1–2k tokens typical responses
- Sustained throughput requirement = ~120 requests/minute (steady-state), with bursts to 350 rpm for 2–3 minute windows
- Concurrent active sessions during peak = 60 simultaneous streams
- Tail/99 latency visibility required for SLA conversations

Key workload notes:
- Mixed chat/generation (40% short replies <128 tokens, 60% longer streaming outputs ~512–1024 tokens)
- KV cache reuse expected for repeated user contexts (estimated cache hit ~30%)
- Sensitive PII; you prefer Private/Dedicated with VPC (we have the security checklist in the HubSpot link)

Validation plan (proposal):
1) Engineering perf run (1.5 hours): reserve a dedicated pool that matches your target concurrency/throughput and run realistic traces (mix above).
2) GPU comparisons: run the same trace on H100 (fp16), A100 (bf16), and L4 (int8) quantized builds for cost/latency tradeoffs.
3) Streaming gating: ensure chunked token flushes maintain P95 < 150ms while sustaining concurrency; record P95/P99 and CPU/GPU utilization.
4) Ops checklist: KV cache toggles, batching windows, and fallback to smaller model under pressure.

Ask from your side: please confirm the burst window assumptions and a 2-hour window availability for an on-site validation run next week (Mon/Tue preferred). Also confirm who from ops will be on the call (cc: ops@brightbridge.ai if different).

Next internal step: looping Dev and Marcus to size the pool and propose a concrete reserved capacity config and expected cost delta.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short sync once you confirm windows.

— Tessa

All — ran the initial microbench and a short pilot. Summary below; full matrix attached. 

Short summary (pilot using 750-token average):
- H100 (fp16): P95 = 120ms, P99 = 260ms, tokens/sec ~ 9.2k, GPU util 68% at 120 rpm steady-state. Handles 5-min burst to 420 rpm with P95 ~170ms (KV cache on).
- A100 (bf16): P95 = 165ms, P99 = 340ms, tokens/sec ~7.8k, GPU util 72% at 120 rpm. Burst to 350 rpm pushes P95 to ~210ms.
- L4 (int8 quant): P95 = 240ms, P99 = 500ms, tokens/sec ~5.5k, GPU util 80% — good cost profile but misses your P95 target for streaming.

KV cache effect: enabling cache improved H100 P95 by ~12% in steady state and reduced tail amplification during bursts. Batching window tweaks (8–12ms) improved GPU throughput without materially affecting P95 streaming chunk flushes.

Recommendation:
- For BrightBridge's SLOs (P95 < 150ms streaming, 60 concurrent), provision a small H100 reserved pool with autoscale headroom (start: 4x H100 nodes, burst policy to add 2 nodes automatically). This gives headroom for 5-minute bursts in testing; cost uplift vs A100 estimated +22% but meets latency.
- If cost pressure is significant and occasional tail degradation is acceptable, use A100 with an aggressive burst fallback to a smaller model (or shorter max tokens) for degraded windows. L4 is not recommended for primary streaming use.

I've attached bb_validation_matrix.csv (detailed results) and perf-logs-20260915.tar.gz (pilot logs).

Next steps: confirm we schedule the 2-hour validation on Tue 2026-09-22 10–12 PT. I can run the full comparative suite that morning and share live dashboards.
